review.notes: Drafted for issue #12. Network: this drafting session could reach only en.wikipedia.org, www.wikidata.org and tiles.openfreemap.org. Refused by the proxy (CONNECT 403 or no connection): www.ibiblio.org (Ellis, Victory in the West vol. I, HyperWar transcription), archive.org and web.archive.org, www.openstreetmap.org, overpass-api.de, nominatim.openstreetmap.org, cgsc.contentdm.oclc.org (Williams 2007 thesis), apps.dtic.mil, www.ddaymuseum.co.uk (Portsmouth Museum Services FAQ), www.cwgc.org, www.iwm.org.uk, www.dday-overlord.com, www.goldbeach.org.uk, fr.wikipedia.org; history.army.mil returned HTTP 403. No official history or named historian was read directly, so every historical cite is to English Wikipedia at a pinned revision; each locator names the work the article cites (mostly Trew 2004, Ford & Zaloga 2009) so the claims can be upgraded once those or Ellis can be read. OSM: openstreetmap.org was unreachable, so OSM-derived data was read from OpenFreeMap vector tiles (planet build 20261122_124456_pt, z14). Tile feature ids are cited as seen; they appear to encode the OSM element (id×10 + 1 node / 2 way / 3 relation, e.g. 9961187072 → way/996118707), but this could not be confirmed on openstreetmap.org, so no `osm` field is set. Geometry: a single representative point on the present-day shoreline at the longitude of the Le Hamel place node, because the 231st Brigade's first wave landed at Le Hamel/Asnelles. No polygon or line: the article says the Jig/King boundary was at strongpoint WN-35, Le Pont Chaussé, but no readable source located Le Pont Chaussé, and Jig's western limit is not described. Sub-beaches Jig Green and Jig Red appear only in image captions, so no separate records. Open questions: Ford & Zaloga (via Wikipedia) say the Hampshires' companies landed 'very close' to Le Hamel, while Trew (via Wikipedia) says both battalions came ashore 'well to the east' of their intended points; both are paraphrased in the summary without reconciling them. The 76 casualties for 47 Commando are agreed by both articles; the 47 Commando article's own source (47commando.org.uk) is a dead link. Sources checked 2026-11-27 by an independent check-sources agent for PR #20: every quote, section locator and cited page verified against the pinned Wikipedia revisions; Le Hamel place feature re-read from the same OpenFreeMap build. Fixes: 47 Commando locators now name both refs on the paragraph (Trew p. 154, Ford & Zaloga p. 289) and the No. 47 Commando article section (§ Operations, not § History). The 1st Hampshires' WN-39 role rests on reading 'D Company' in § Jig Sector as a Hampshires company, which the paragraph implies.

summary.text: The western of Gold's two assault sectors, in front of Le Hamel and Asnelles. The 1st Dorsets and 1st Hampshires of the 231st Infantry Brigade landed first, east of their intended points because of navigation errors and the current, and were met by fire from a casemated 75 mm gun at Le Hamel that covered the beach. Their supporting DD and Centaur tanks arrived late and many bogged down or were knocked out. The Hampshires took strongpoint WN-36 at the east of Asnelles but had to work round Le Hamel from the rear; an AVRE silenced the gun in the afternoon, after which the Hampshires cleared strongpoints westward to the Arromanches radar station. The 2nd Devons landed later in the morning and went inland to take Ryes, and the Dorsets swung west onto the high ground south of Arromanches, which fell late in the afternoon. No. 47 (Royal Marine) Commando also came ashore here, losing several landing craft, before setting off for Port-en-Bessin.
